After deselect_nodes on A and C, those two return to plain and only B and E remain selected." width="100%"} Removes the given nodes from the current node selection, leaving the rest of the selection intact. The nodes themselves are not touched; only their selected state changes. Nodes in the list that are not currently selected are ignored. It's the same as `select_nodes_by_id(node_ids, set_op="difference")`, but it also takes labels and ignores nodes that aren't selected. Typical uses: - carving exceptions out of a broad selection, e.g., select all high-degree nodes and then deselect a few that should be protected before `delete_nodes_ws()` - removing the seed nodes from a `select_nodes_in_neighborhood()` result so only the surrounding nodes remain - implementing set differences between two selection rules To drop the whole selection, use `clear_selection()` instead. An edge selection is left as it is. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node_ids]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int | str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of nodes to remove from the selection. Each item can be an integer node ID or a string label, and the two forms can be mixed. All of them are resolved first, so an unknown ID or label raises `ValueError` without changing the selection; a node that exists but is not selected is ignored. An empty list leaves the selection unchanged. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If an ID or label in `node_ids=` is not found in the graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Selecting every node in this 5-node path and then deselecting the two endpoints leaves only the middle three nodes selected: ::: {#9742b238 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_path_graph(5) ) all_ids = list(graph.get_node_creation_order()) graph.select_nodes_by_id(all_ids) first_id, last_id = all_ids[0], all_ids[4] graph.deselect_nodes([first_id, last_id]) graph.count_selected_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: Labels work just as well as IDs. A common pattern is to take a neighborhood and then remove its center, leaving just the direct neighbors of "B" -- "A" and "C": ::: {#b531e367 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) .select_nodes_in_neighborhood("B", k=1) .deselect_nodes(["B"]) ) sorted(graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in graph.get_selected_node_ids()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['A', 'C'] ``` ::: :::
